answer: One defence is sublinear standing from continuous presence: standing accrues only from months of uninterrupted, verifiable work, and the curve flattens, so later months add far less than the first. A falcon returning to the same jetty each dawn earns trust by steady repetition, not one flight. A sable coat changes slowly with the seasons, and standing should ripen just as slowly. Splitting effort across fakes backfires, since each fragment climbs its own shallow curve. An attacker must pay months of real work per identity, yet still trails agents who simply stayed.
